items.stem: A small business cannot find where to install plugins and custom themes on their WordPress.com-hosted site. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: Plugin and theme installation is restricted on lower WordPress.com plans; the self-hosted software allows it fully
options.rationale: Correct: the hosted service limits extensibility on some plans, unlike a self-hosted WordPress install.

options.text: Plugins no longer exist in WordPress
options.rationale: Plugins exist; the limitation is the hosting tier.
An expired domain would take the whole site offline, not just hide plugin options.
The browser is unrelated to plan-level feature limits.

items.stem: Which TWO practices most reduce the risk of losing a WordPress site to a failed update or attack? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: restorable backups let you recover from a bad update or compromise.

options.text: Applying core, theme and plugin updates promptly
options.rationale: Correct: timely updates close known vulnerabilities.

options.text: Adding as many plugins as possible
options.rationale: More plugins increase the attack surface and maintenance burden.
The title has no bearing on security or recovery.

items.explanation: Correct: restorable backups let you recover from a bad update or compromise.

items.stem: A content editor wants the same styled call-to-action block on ten pages and the ability to update it everywhere at once. What is the best approach?

options.text: Create it once as a reusable/synced pattern and insert that pattern on each page
options.rationale: Correct: a synced pattern is edited in one place and updates every instance.

options.text: Copy and paste the block onto each page separately
options.rationale: Copies must each be edited individually, defeating the goal.

options.text: Install a new plugin for every page
options.rationale: That adds overhead and does not provide shared editing.

options.text: Write the HTML by hand on each page
options.rationale: Hand-coding ten copies is error-prone and not centrally editable.

items.explanation: Correct: a synced pattern is edited in one place and updates every instance.
